findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permissions, encoding)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use .map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is hidden side-effect I/O inside a mapping closure that should be pure calculation
findings.failure_mode: pure domain logic leaks logging into the core; output becomes non-deterministic and side effects cannot be controlled or tested
findings.fix: move all println to the shell boundary; return log data in the result type if the caller needs it

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 silently truncates any value >65535
findings.failure_mode: external input value 70000 parses to u32 then truncates to 44716 with no error, corrupting domain data
findings.fix: use u16::from_str_radix or try_from(u32) with .map_err to return a typed Overflow/ParseError

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(..).collect() allocates an intermediate Vec and splits on every comma; uses parts[0] and parts[1] indexing
findings.failure_mode: every line allocates a Vec of String copies; out-of-bounds indexing panics on malformed lines; alloc().collect() pattern is forbidden for simple two-field records
findings.fix: use let (_name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; then parse value_str.trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid)

findings.problem: function returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures collapse into unwrap() panics
findings.failure_mode: missing file, empty line, non-numeric value, and out-of-range value are indistinguishable at the call site; caller cannot recover or report
findings.fix: define enum LoadError { Io(std::io::Error), Invalid, Overflow }; return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: load_sessions fuses file I/O, string parsing, logging, allocation, and domain Record construction into one function
findings.failure_mode: Data/Calculations/Actions boundary is violated; shell (fs, println) is mixed with calculation (parsing, struct construction), making core untestable in isolation
findings.fix: split into shell fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> { let text = fs::read_to_string(path)?; parse_records(&text) } and pure fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: .map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() builds a Vec<String> per line for a two-field record
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line increases memory pressure and allocation count; each line copies the string twice (to Vec then to Record fields)
findings.fix: use split_once to get (&str, &str) directly; clone only the two fields needed into Record with .to_string() on the final values

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] access Vec elements without bounds checking on untrusted input lines
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than two commas panics at runtime with index out of bounds
findings.fix: use split_once which returns Option, and .ok_or() to convert to a typed error

findings.problem: load_sessions has no max-rows cap, no try_reserve, and no input size validation before collecting into Vec
findings.failure_mode: a large file causes unbounded heap allocation that can OOM the process with no graceful degradation
findings.fix: accept a max_rows: usize parameter, validate line count or use try_reserve(max_rows).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation), and enforce the cap per push

findings.problem: raw String and u32 from split and parse cross the parse boundary without a fallible smart constructor into a trusted domain value
findings.failure_mode: callers (and intermediate code) can construct Record with any name string and any truncated u16 value, including invalid states that the domain should reject
findings.fix: introduce a ParseError::Invalid/Overflow and use split_once + fallible u16 parse so that only valid Records are constructible

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 - parsing to wrong width (u32) then narrowing lossily to u16 violates checked conversion rule
findings.failure_mode: value 70000 fits in u32, parses successfully, truncates to 44716 in u16 silently; domain receives incorrect data without error
findings.fix: parse directly as u16: parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid), or use u16::try_from(u32_val).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow)

The crate violates panic freedom (unwrap on I/O and parse), hidden I/O (println in core), lossy casts (u32 as u16), intermediate allocation (split.collect), unchecked indexing (parts[0]/parts[1]), no bounded allocation, no typed error taxonomy, and no functional core separation.
